Avery / Ben — quick read below. I annotated the PDF (see redline_summary_notes.txt) but the high-level positions:

- Notice period: 30 days is too short for complex infringement claims where we need to assess model provenance and match training data; propose 90 days for notice with a good-faith obligation to provide interim information within 30 days.

- Defense / control: we should not concede automatic defense control for third-party IP claims. Offer a hybrid: Redwood can assume defense for claims that directly implicate our model outputs (and we retain right to select counsel), but both parties share approval on material settlements. For claims alleging customer misuse of output, customer retains control.

- Cap: 12 months of fees is commercially reasonable only if coupled with an insurance floor or an escrow holdback. Counter: cap at 12 months of fees + $1M insurance floor OR offer limited escrow (6 months of fees held in escrow, released after 12 months if no covered claim).

- OSS carveout: Acceptable with narrow language — only for dependencies identified in a bill-of-materials attached to the order form.

- Evidence & subpoenas: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and KMS architecture diagram; we cannot provide raw training data or unredacted logs without a subpoena or court order.

Action items: Ben — draft a short commercial note for the customer with the compromise options and pricing impact. Avery — I recommend offering the hybrid defense/control + 90-day notice + escrow/insurance combo as our first counter.
